relations.subject: server:swap-rebalance
relations.evidence: If you add one node to the cluster and remove a node during the same rebalance, Couchbase Server will do a "swap rebalance". This means data and indexes from the node being removed are moved to the one being added.

relations.subject: service:search-service
relations.evidence: A comma separated list of nodes to add the Search Service to.

notable_absence.finding: Rebalance is a cluster-wide, potentially long-running and disruptive operation (it can add/remove services from nodes and trigger a full swap rebalance), yet no specific RBAC role or privilege is ever named as required to invoke it - only the generic 'unauthorized error' boilerplate shared by every couchbase-cli subcommand appears. This is consistent across the whole batch.

cross_component_finding: The six --<service>-add/--<service>-remove flag pairs (fts/index/query/backup/analytics/eventing) each describe adding or removing 'the Search Service' / 'the Index Service' etc. in near-identical one-line prose, differing only in the service name - a templated pattern rather than independently composed descriptions, consistent with this round's lighter-TW-review authorship hypothesis. The --fts-add/--fts-remove flag names spell the service 'fts' while the prose calls it 'the Search Service' - the same CLI-flag-vs-service-name split already documented in the registry's promoted service:search-service note (from couchbase-cli-cluster-init.json's --cluster-fts-ramsize flag), reinforcing rather than introducing that terminology-drift finding. The entire HOST FORMATS, CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION (MTLS AUTHENTICATION), and ENVIRONMENT AND CONFIGURATION VARIABLES sections are reproduced verbatim - the same boilerplate seen on essentially every other couchbase-cli page in this and prior rounds.
cross_product_finding: Not addressed on this page - no comparison to Capella is made. Rebalance on Capella is a fully managed background operation with no customer-facing CLI equivalent, so this entire page's flag surface (manual service placement per node, swap rebalance, --no-wait/--no-progress-bar) has no Capella analogue to compare against.
